Subject: Re: [URGENT] Lucent production: sustained latency + 5xx spike on dedicated pool

Anita / Jordan — short technical readout from the SRE triage: we are observing the following on Lucent’s dedicated pool (pool-id: lucent-prod-03):

- Symptom summary: sustained increase in KV-cache churn and continuous-batch queue depth starting 07:50 PST; 95th pct token latency rose to 1.1–1.3s; 5xx spike correlates with OOM-like retries on a subset of hosts.
- Root hypothesis: a shard of your pool moved to a kernel path that uses a different attention kernel (recent optimizer change on our side) and is not honoring the previous per-tenant concurrency heuristics; the result is higher per-request memory pressure and reduced effective throughput on ~18% of hosts.
- Why reserved throughput looks short: autoscaler is capping because the hosts are reporting unhealthy kernel-level metrics; scheduler avoids packing more load there which reduces visible committed throughput even though the logical reservation still exists. That’s why you see queued requests despite 'reserved' capacity.

Immediate mitigations attempted (status):
- Blacklist problematic hosts from routing (in progress) — should reduce 5xx immediately (ETA 10m).
- Rollback kernel-selector flag to previous stable path for affected shard (in progress) — ETA 25m for canary + 30m to fully converge.
- If rollback doesn’t restore capacity quickly, we will spin an emergency temporary pool and route a portion of traffic there — provisioning ETA 20–25m, route cutover + testing 15m.

Requested authorization: Jordan, can we get authorization to provision a temporary 4-GPU burst pool under Lucent’s account and bill to the usual overage path? This will remove immediate queuing while kernel fix proceeds.

I’m attaching a brief log excerpt and the qps snapshot you sent for traceability.

—David Kim
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
